## Summit Therapeutics Provides Update Regarding Ivonescimab Biologics License Application


November 15, 2026


- [Download (opens in new window)](https://s206.q4cdn.com/652410165/files/doc_news/Summit-Therapeutics-Provides-Update-Regarding-Ivonescimab-Biologics-License-Application-2026.pdf)


*Complete Response Letter Received from FDA for BLA Application Based on HARMONi Study*


MIAMI--(BUSINESS WIRE)--


Summit Therapeutics Inc. (NASDAQ: SMMT) today announced that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has issued a Complete Response Letter (CRL) regarding the Biologics License Application (BLA) for ivonescimab in combination with platinum-containing chemotherapy for the treatment of patients with locally advanced or metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), who have received prior epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) therapy. Ivonescimab is a novel PD-1 x VEGF bispecific antibody.


“As a cancer survivor, I understand firsthand how important it is for patients to have access to multiple treatment options, particularly when they are facing diseases with significant unmet medical needs,” emphasized Dr. Maky Zanganeh, President and Co-Chief Executive Officer of Summit Therapeutics. “Behind every diagnosis is a person, a family, and a community hoping for more time, more possibilities, and a better future. I know that hope is not simply an emotion; it is the possibility that another treatment, another scientific breakthrough, or another therapeutic option may make a meaningful difference in someone’s life. Every additional treatment option matters. It represents another opportunity for patients and their families, especially those who have exhausted existing therapies or have limited alternatives. Our responsibility as an industry is to continue advancing science, challenging conventional thinking, and bringing innovative medicines to patients in need. For me, our mission is deeply personal to bring our innovative medicine to patients who may benefit most.”


The CRL indicates that the BLA cannot be approved in its present form, as the FDA determined that substantial evidence of effectiveness is not established in the absence of a statistically significant overall survival (OS) improvement. The FDA indicated that the progression-free survival (PFS) benefit in the absence of a statistically significant OS benefit does not support a positive benefit-risk profile in support of approval.


Currently, there are no FDA-approved regimens that have demonstrated a statistically significant OS benefit in this patient setting. In the primary analysis for OS, ivonescimab in combination with chemotherapy showed a positive trend without achieving a statistically significant result. In a post-hoc analysis, longer-term follow-up of western patients demonstrated a consistent OS benefit across regions with a hazard ratio of 0.76 in the full population, the Asian patients, and the western patients.


The BLA was supported by data from[HARMONi](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fclinicaltrials.gov%2Fstudy%2FNCT06396065&esheet=54641467&newsitemid=20261115117181&lan=en-US&anchor=HARMONi&index=1&md5=9a80144bba0dba0bbe81ec56933be70d) , a global, randomized, double-blind Phase III clinical trial evaluating ivonescimab combined with platinum-containing chemotherapy compared with placebo combined with platinum-containing chemotherapy in patients with EGFR-mutated, locally advanced or metastatic non-squamous NSCLC who were previously treated with a third-generation EGFR TKI. The HARMONi study has two primary endpoints: PFS and OS. HARMONi met its PFS primary endpoint, becoming the first global Phase III study of an immunotherapy-based regimen to show a statistically significant PFS improvement in this setting. The primary PFS analysis was also supported by longer-term follow-up in a post-hoc analysis, which demonstrated a consistent magnitude of benefit with more mature data of western patients.


Ivonescimab in combination with chemotherapy demonstrated an acceptable and manageable safety profile, which was consistent with previous studies. Ivonescimab plus chemotherapy was well-tolerated with no new safety signals and comparable rates of discontinuation and death between both arms. There were 16 patients (7.3%) who discontinued ivonescimab due to treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs) compared to 11 patients (5.0%) who discontinued placebo due to TRAEs. There were four patients (1.8%) in the ivonescimab plus chemotherapy arm and five patients (2.3%) in the chemotherapy alone arm who died as a result of TRAEs in this Phase III study.


“We are disappointed for patients and their families awaiting additional treatment options in this setting,” said Robert W. Duggan, Chairman and Co-Chief Executive Officer of Summit. “We chose to pursue an ivonescimab regimen here based on the opportunity to provide another treatment option to help patients in need. In doing so, we believe the global HARMONi study provided the basis for a treatment option that these patients needed.”


“With five positive Phase III studies between Summit and Akeso, nothing changes with respect to our ever-growing belief in the opportunity for ivonescimab and our determination to advance ivonescimab’s development,” continued Robert Duggan. “Our mission remains to improve outcomes for patients facing significant unmet needs, which is work worth doing, and we will continue through our expansive clinical development program.”


Summit is currently developing ivonescimab in NSCLC, colorectal cancer (CRC), urothelial carcinoma (UC), and renal cell carcinoma (RCC), specifically conducting multiregional Phase II or Phase III clinical trials in the following proposed indications or settings beyond the HARMONi study:


- HARMONi-3 (Phase III): ivonescimab combined with chemotherapy in patients with first-line metastatic NSCLC, with two distinct cohorts to be analyzed separately for squamous tumors and non-squamous tumors;


- HARMONi-7 (Phase III): ivonescimab monotherapy in patients with first-line metastatic NSCLC whose tumors have high PD-L1 expression;


- HARMONi-GI3 (Phase III): ivonescimab combined with chemotherapy in patients with first-line unresectable metastatic CRC;


- HARMONi-GU1 (Phase II / III): ivonescimab plus the antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) enfortumab vedotin (EV) in previously untreated patients with first-line metastatic UC; and


- SMT112-216 (Phase II): multiple ivonescimab-based combination treatment regimens in first-line patients with metastatic clear cell RCC (ccRCC) (SMT112-216 is also referred to as AK112-216 in China).


In addition, Summit is collaborating with other biopharmaceutical companies to test ivonescimab in combination with other novel compounds, including with:


- AstraZeneca and Daiichi Sankyo, planning to combine ivonescimab with DATROWAY® (datopotamab deruxtecan), a TROP-2 targeted ADC, in breast cancer and lung cancer, including the intent to initiate a Phase III study in first-line triple-negative breast cancer;


- AstraZeneca, planning to combine ivonescimab with the novel Claudin 18.2 targeted ADC, sonesitatug vedotin, in multiple gastrointestinal tumors;


- Revolution Medicines, combining ivonescimab with multiple RAS(ON) inhibitors, including a multi-selective inhibitor RASONQUE® (daraxonrasib), a G12D-selective inhibitor zoldonrasib, and a G12C-selective inhibitor elironrasib in multiple solid tumor settings;


- GSK, combining ivonescimab with the novel B7-H3 targeted ADC, risvutatug rezetecan, in multiple solid tumor settings; and


- Arcus Biosciences, planning to combine ivonescimab with the novel HIF-2α inhibitor, casdatifan, in ccRCC.


Finally, Summit is collaborating with two cooperative groups to evaluate ivonescimab in Phase III studies including biliary tract cancer (BTC) and head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC), including with:


- GORTEC, a European Head and Neck Oncology and Radiotherapy Group based in France, to evaluate ivonescimab monotherapy and ivonescimab in combination with ligufalimab, Akeso’s proprietary anti-CD47 monoclonal antibody, against monotherapy pembrolizumab in a randomized three-arm study in first-line advanced HNSCC. The Phase III study, GORTEC 2024-04 ILLUMINE (NCT07264075), is sponsored by GORTEC and is intended to be conducted in multiple countries in Europe and in China; Summit may consider the expansion of this study into the United States; and


- ECOG-ACRIN Cancer Research Group to evaluate ivonescimab in combination with chemotherapy compared to pembrolizumab or durvalumab in combination with chemotherapy in first-line advanced BTC in a registration-enabling Phase II / III clinical study, EA2251.


Ivonescimab is an investigational therapy that is not approved by any regulatory authority in Summit’s license territories, including the United States and Europe. Ivonescimab was initially approved for marketing authorization in China in May 2024. Currently, there are no PD-1 x VEGF bispecific antibodies approved in the U.S.


**About Ivonescimab**


Ivonescimab, known as SMT112 in Summit’s license territories, North America, South America, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, and Japan, and as AK112 outside of Summit’s license territories, is a novel, potential first-in-class investigational bispecific antibody combining the effects of immunotherapy via a blockade of PD-1 with the anti-angiogenesis effects associated with blocking VEGF into a single molecule. By design, ivonescimab displays unique cooperative binding to each of its intended targets with multifold higher affinity to PD-1 when in the presence of VEGF.


This design is intended to differentiate ivonescimab as there is potentially higher expression (presence) of both PD-1 and VEGF in tumor tissue and the tumor microenvironment (TME) as compared to normal tissue in the body. Summit believes ivonescimab’s specifically engineered tetravalent structure (four binding sites) enables higher avidity (accumulated strength of multiple binding interactions) in the TME (Zhong, *et al* , iScience, 2025). This tetravalent structure, the intentional novel design of the molecule, and bringing these two targets into a single bispecific antibody with cooperative binding qualities have the potential to direct ivonescimab to the tumor tissue versus healthy tissue. The intent of this design, together with a half-life of 6 to 7 days after the first dose (Zhong, *et al* , iScience, 2025) increasing to approximately 10 days at steady state dosing, is to improve upon previously established efficacy thresholds, side effects, and safety profiles associated with prior approved drugs to these targets.


Ivonescimab was invented by Akeso Inc. (HKEX Code: 9926.HK) and is currently utilized in multiple Phase III clinical trials. Over 5,000 patients have been treated with ivonescimab in clinical studies globally, and over 100,000 patients when considering those treated in a commercial setting in China, as noted by Akeso.


Ivonescimab is an investigational therapy that is not approved by any regulatory authority in Summit’s license territories, including the United States and Europe. Ivonescimab was initially approved for marketing authorization in China in May 2024.


**About Summit Therapeutics Inc.**


Summit Therapeutics Inc. is a biopharmaceutical oncology company focused on the discovery, development, and commercialization of patient-, physician-, caregiver- and societal-friendly medicinal therapies intended to improve quality of life, increase potential duration of life, and resolve serious unmet medical needs.


Summit was founded in 2003 and the company’s shares are listed on the Nasdaq Global Market (symbol "SMMT"). Summit is headquartered in Miami, Florida, with additional offices in Palo Alto, California, Princeton, New Jersey, Dublin, Ireland, and Oxford, UK.
